chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Uthman ibn Isa who linked it up through a chain of narrations to Aba Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
If one takes a female slave and doesn’t have sex with her once every forty days, he would be held responsible for her sins.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a master does not have intercourse with his female slave for forty days?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal outlines the master's responsibility to provide sexual relief to his female slave to prevent her from committing zina, a ruling derived from the principle of preventing harm. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes a specific obligation (wajib) on the owner, distinguishing it from general rights of concubinage, and highlights the social context of slavery in early Islamic society where sexual access was a primary right of ownership.
